title: What Computer Vision Can Do · Level 3
slo: Identify the computer vision technique that fits a simple workplace image task.

options.rationale: Correct. Computer vision processes visual input such as images, videos, and live camera streams.

options.text: AI that predicts one image label
options.error_type: confuses computer vision with image classification
options.rationale: Not quite. Predicting one label for a main subject is image classification, which is one vision task.
options.better_fit: Choose this when one image needs one main-subject label, such as apple or banana.

feedback.intrinsic: A camera task could be narrowed too early to just one kind of result.
feedback.instructional: Computer vision is the broader area for processing visual input; image classification is only one task within it.

options.error_type: confuses computer vision with semantic segmentation
options.rationale: Not quite. Labeling individual pixels describes semantic segmentation, a more precise location task.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the needed result is the exact pixels belonging to objects.

feedback.intrinsic: A simple visual task could be mistaken for one needing pixel-level detail.
feedback.instructional: Semantic segmentation is a specific vision technique. Computer vision includes it and many other techniques.

options.text: A model that combines images and text
options.error_type: confuses a broad AI area with a multimodal model
options.rationale: Not quite. Combining images and text describes a multimodal model, not the whole visual-processing area.
options.better_fit: Choose this when image information and written language are used together.

feedback.intrinsic: The task could be limited to image-and-language work even when visual processing is broader.
feedback.instructional: A multimodal model is one kind of model. Computer vision is the broader area that processes visual input.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Computer vision covers processing visual input to produce useful meaning or insights.

exercises.question_text: Contextual image analysis can suggest relevant tags for an image.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A photo could miss useful labels that describe its content.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Contextual image analysis finds relationships between image objects and descriptive text, so it can suggest tags.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Suggesting relevant tags is one result of interpreting visual content with language.

exercises.question_text: A multimodal model uses only one kind of information, such as images alone.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: A written product description could be ignored when it should be considered with the photo.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: A multimodal model combines more than one kind of information, such as images and text.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Multimodal means that more than one modality is combined.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence no longer shows how examining regions leads to location results.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the technique, then what it examines, followed by what it finds.

exercises.correct_answer: Object detection examines multiple regions to find objects and their locations
exercises.explanation: The technique checks multiple image regions for possible objects. Its result includes both the objects found and their locations.

exercises.question_text: Semantic segmentation uses rectangular bounding boxes as its precise object location result.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: An exact item outline would be confused with a broad rectangular area.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Semantic segmentation assigns individual pixels to objects, making its locations more precise than bounding boxes.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Bounding boxes are used in object detection, while segmentation classifies pixels.

exercises.question_text: Which inputs can computer vision software process? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Digital photographs are visual input that computer vision can process.
Correct. Videos are visual input that computer vision can process.
Correct. A live camera stream is visual input that computer vision can process.

options.error_type: confuses visual input with text labels
options.rationale: Not quite. Written labels can describe images, but they are not the only visual input processed.
options.better_fit: Choose this for a task focused only on written language rather than visual input.

feedback.intrinsic: A camera or photograph would be left out of the task.
feedback.instructional: Computer vision processes images, videos, and live camera streams. Labels may be results or accompanying text.

exercises.explanation: Correct. All three are forms of visual input that can be processed.

exercises.question_text: Put the pieces in the correct order.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The idea no longer clearly connects training images with the label produced.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Put the technique first, then its labeled training images, followed by the one-label prediction.

exercises.correct_answer: Image classification uses labeled images to predict one main-subject label
exercises.explanation: Training images provide correct names for the model to learn from. The resulting prediction is one label for the image's main subject.

exercises.question_text: A smart-checkout designer must scan several products in one basket image. The store needs each product type and a rectangular coordinate area, but not an exact pixel outline. Which approach is best?

options.rationale: Correct. It finds multiple product types and reports rectangular coordinate locations.

options.error_type: confuses several located objects with one image label
options.rationale: Not quite. Image classification predicts one main-subject label and does not locate each product.
options.better_fit: Choose this when a photo contains one main item and needs one type label.

feedback.intrinsic: Several basket products could be treated as one main subject.
feedback.instructional: The need for each product and a rectangular area points to object detection.

options.error_type: chooses pixel-level location instead of bounding boxes
options.rationale: Not quite. Semantic segmentation gives a more precise pixel-level location than the requested rectangles.
options.better_fit: Choose this when exact object pixels are needed instead of rectangular areas.

feedback.intrinsic: The checkout design could require unnecessary outline-level detail.
feedback.instructional: Bounding boxes are rectangular coordinate areas from object detection. Semantic segmentation classifies pixels.

options.error_type: confuses location reporting with image descriptions
options.rationale: Not quite. Contextual image analysis interprets images and can generate descriptions or tags.
options.better_fit: Choose this when the basket image needs a written description or tags.

feedback.intrinsic: The store could get descriptive language without rectangular areas for each product.
feedback.instructional: Object detection gives object types and locations. Contextual analysis focuses on image-and-language interpretation.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The needed output is several product types with bounding-box locations.

exercises.question_text: A grocery-store manager reviews a produce-scale design. Each photo has one centered fruit, and the checkout needs its type, not an outline or coordinates. Which reasons support image classification? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. One centered fruit is the image's main subject, so one label fits.

options.text: It can label the fruit apple or banana
options.rationale: Correct. Fruit names are labels image classification can predict.

options.text: It does not require pixel-by-pixel location
options.rationale: Correct. The task asks for a type and does not need precise object pixels.

options.text: It gives a precise pixel outline
options.error_type: confuses image classification with semantic segmentation
options.rationale: Not quite. Precise pixel location is produced by semantic segmentation.
options.better_fit: Choose this when an item's exact pixel-level outline is required.

feedback.intrinsic: The scale would seek detail beyond the fruit type needed for checkout.
feedback.instructional: Image classification gives one label. Semantic segmentation classifies each pixel for more precise location.

exercises.explanation: Correct. A single fruit type is the needed result, without coordinates or pixel-level location.

exercises.question_text: Models that connect image objects with descriptive text can perform ___.

parts.text: Models that connect image objects with descriptive text can perform

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The image could be given only a label or a model category instead of the requested interpretation task.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use contextual image analysis for interpreting image-and-text relationships. Image classification predicts one label; a multimodal model combines information types.

exercises.explanation: Connecting visual objects with descriptive text enables scene interpretation, descriptions, and relevant tags. Image classification gives one label, while multimodal model names the model type that can combine modalities.

exercises.question_text: A product-photo editor needs the exact outline of each item in a photo, not rectangles or one overall label. Which reasons support semantic segmentation? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Classifying individual pixels supports an exact item outline.

options.text: It gives more precise locations than boxes
options.rationale: Correct. Pixel classification is more precise than rectangular bounding boxes.

options.text: It assigns pixels to their objects
options.rationale: Correct. Each pixel is classified based on the object it belongs to.

options.error_type: confuses semantic segmentation with image classification
options.rationale: Not quite. One main-subject label does not provide an outline for every item.
options.better_fit: Choose this when only the main subject's type is needed.

feedback.intrinsic: The editor would lack the exact item outlines needed for the photo.
feedback.instructional: One label is image classification. Semantic segmentation assigns pixels to objects for precise locations.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Exact outlines require classifying pixels rather than using boxes or one overall label.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence no longer clearly shows what information is combined and why.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Begin with the model, then join images with text, and finish with the visual-language purpose.

exercises.correct_answer: A multimodal model combines images with text to link visual language
exercises.explanation: The defining feature is combining image and text information. That combination supports relationships between visual content and language.
